body: Apparently, enabling/disabling rules through comments for configurable rules doesn't work at all... Trying to fix that now.

I kind of think we need two behaviors:
1. There must be an array for configurable rules to specify more than just the error level.
2. If there isn't an array, the value is considered to be the error level.

That way, you can change error level without changing the other options.

@nzakas Point 2, do you mean that if we pass non-array into a rule that is configurable (i.e. takes an array), we should only override an error level? Does the same behavior should apply to local configs? If main config file specifies `quotes: [2, 'single']` and local config specifies `quotes:1` should they be merged into `quotes: [1, 'single']`? I've fixed the code already to handle unexpected values as a parameter, but I need to fix it to work with arrays, and that requires some complex tweaks to RegEx that parses comments.

Yes, that's what I mean. If it's not an array, then it should be an error
level.

For parsing the comments, can you simplify into something like this:

function makeObject(comment) {

```
// strip of /*eslint and */

var code = "{" + comment + "}",

return (new Function("'use strict'; return " + code))();
```

}

So you basically end up doing a kind of eval?

Ahh.. very nice idea! Didn't think of that myself. Spent last hour beating my head against negative lookarounds in RegEx and getting nowhere... I'll change the code for it tomorrow. I probably will have to separate parsing code for globals from rules enabling/disabling, but that's ok, I think.

I just tried your suggested approach. It doesn't work with something like `/* eslint: no-alert: 1 */` because it's evaluating `-` as a minus... Any suggestions? JSON.Parse also doesn't work due to not having quotes around rule names. Should we just require quotes around rule names for comments?

I don't want to require quotes around the rules, it's yucky. :) We could do
a simply regex replacement of something like

text.replace(/([a-z0-9-]+):/g, "\"$1\":");

Then use the function approach?
@nzakas: That's a little too naive. It will replace inside strings given as options.
Is that true? The colon is unique to the rule name, is it not?

body: Pull requested. I can't say that I like the code to do this... But I think it should work.
We don't have configurations with colons. :)
Not yet. Also, eslint allows users to define their own rules, and we can't assume that they will not parameterise their custom rules by strings containing colons.

We can fix that by conventions easily. "Don't do it" :)

moot point now, Ilya already fixed this.
@michaelficarra I agree that this is not the best way to do this, but I couldn't find better approach outside of coding a full tokenizer for comments...

Let's not worry too much more about this right now. I'm happy with the
progress, and I fully expect people to mostly use .eslintrc files to
specify their options.
